title: How Lenny grew a paid newsletter to 3,000+ subscribers: quality content, guest posts, and staying simple
summary: Lenny explains how he went from leaving Airbnb with no plan to a six-figure paid newsletter. He covers early growth via Twitter and high-quality guest posts, pricing, free-to-paid conversion, a sustainable writing process, and why he deliberately keeps the business small and simple.

principles.text: Anything not spent creating high-quality content barely moves newsletter growth; value drives word of mouth.
principles.quote: i find there's any time not spent creating high quality content is not time well spent and i just keep finding it over and over

principles.text: Guest post early, putting your best work where the audience already is, to jump-start your first thousand subscribers.
principles.quote: you just want to go to where your audience is and if you can write something that in a place somebody already has that whole audience and show how awesome you are they're gonna come follow you wherever you are

principles.text: Price higher than you think you should (he settled on $15/month), then discount occasionally with holiday deals.
principles.quote: priced higher than you think you should everybody always wants to start at five bucks a month because that's the lowest you can go and no one ever thinks their stuff is worth it

principles.text: Share drafts with supporters and peers before launching so they give feedback and then promote it.
principles.quote: i ran it by folks like andrew chan and and a bunch of other people with a large twitter following like generally to get their feedback on how to frame the announcement because they were supporters along the way and then also it led to them tweeting about it

principles.text: Write mostly what you're curious about (about 80%) with 20% for what readers want, or you'll burn out.
principles.quote: i try to do like a 80 what do i actually care about this week and i'm excited to write about with a 20 of like well people care about it this week

principles.text: Keep the business simple instead of scaling headcount and business units, to avoid becoming a workaholic again.
principles.quote: i feel like i could make more just keeping it my own thing not hiring anyone full-time not trying to you know add more business units to it
